title: Directive 2013/34/EU on the annual financial statements, consolidated financial statements and related reports of certain types of undertakings
source: Directive 2013/34/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 2013, OJ L 182, 29.6.2013, p. 19, CELEX 32013L0034: Art. 3(2) (small undertakings), 4(1), 9(5), 10, 13, 14, 16(1), 30(1) and 33, Annexes III and V. Read 2026-10-09.
note: The frame each member state carries into its own law; Sweden's is årsredovisningslagen (1995:1554). A drafting check, not accounting advice.

rules.text: The annual financial statements are one whole: at least a balance sheet, a profit and loss account and notes.
Each balance sheet and profit and loss item shows the figure for the preceding year.
The balance sheet follows the layout of Annex III or IV.
The profit and loss account follows Annex V (by nature of expense) or VI (by function).
A small undertaking may show an abridged balance sheet with only the lettered and roman-numbered items, and combine the first items of the profit and loss account into a gross result.
The notes disclose the accounting policies adopted.
The notes give the total of commitments, guarantees and contingencies outside the balance sheet, and any security given.
The notes give debts due after more than five years and debts secured on the undertaking's assets.
The notes give the average number of employees during the year.

A small undertaking stays under two of three limits: a balance sheet total of EUR 5 million, net turnover of EUR 10 million and 50 employees on average (member states may raise the first two) (Art. 3(2) as amended by Delegated Directive (EU) 2023/2775, for financial years from 1 January 2024).
The board answers for the statements together, so the report carries the signatures of those who draw it up.
The approved statements are published within twelve months of the balance sheet date; the report says nothing of having been filed.
